text:
Alex W: quick note — I ran a focused region cost arbitrage/runbook for inference clusters yesterday between ORD and AMS, wanted to surface findings and proposed placement rules
Maria T: awesome, drop the topline pls. is this for hosted API or dedicated pools?
Alex W: dedicated pools (reserved + spot mix). sampled 2 weeks of steady-state traffic: mix of low-latency small chat (p99 target ~120ms) and background batch embeddings
Sahil (infra): curious which instance types you compared and if you normalized for local disk/network egress?
Alex W: compared RTX A6000-equivalent reserved SKU vs T4-ish spot SKU across regions; normalized for egress by including cross-region transfer at $0.02/token-equivalent (back-of-envelope).
Jim K: can you paste the query or command you used?
Alex W: sure — here's the billing join I ran against billing_metrics
```sql
SELECT region, sku_family, SUM(gpu_hours) AS hours, SUM(cost_usd) as cost
FROM billing_metrics
WHERE ts BETWEEN '2026-02-28' AND '2026-03-13'
GROUP BY region, sku_family
ORDER BY cost DESC;
```
Maria T: nice. rough numbers?
Alex W: TL;DR: AMS reserve unit cost ~12% cheaper than ORD for reserved A6000 baseline, but effective per-token latency margin is 18-25ms worse from AMS to our eu-west edge pool. Spot availability in ORD is stronger during EU business hours (fewer preemptions).
Nina F: do you include networking egress and inter-region NAT costs? sometimes those flip the math.
Alex W: yes — included egress between region pairs and VPC NAT+load balancer incremental per-hour. For serving-heavy traffic (many small requests) egress dominates. For embeddings batch (large payloads) the compute math dominates and AMS favours slightly.
Ravi S: what's the SLA impact? if p99 jumps above 120ms we lose product SLO for some customers.
Sahil (infra): measured tail latency from eu-west PoP -> region: ORD p99 ~110ms, AMS p99 ~135ms. we can shave ~15ms with local caching but not for fresh tokens.
Jim K: ops-bot kicked with capacity alerts recently in AMS, right?
ops-bot: ALERT 1767248123: AMS spot churn spike: preemptions increased 2.7x at 2026-03-08T15:12Z — affected 7/24 nodes for ~12m, fallback to reserved pool triggered.
Maria T: if AMS cheaper but less reliable, maybe hybrid rule: latency-critical live inference -> ORD reserved; batch embedding/low-SLO -> AMS reserved+spot. That keeps cost down without impacting SLAs.
Nina F: can finance commit to a 6- or 12-month reservation for AMS if it reduces unit cost significantly? we prefer predictability.
Ravi S: 6-month commit gets us ~9% price drop; 12-month ~16%. but there's a minimum commit size.
Alex W: propose concrete placement rules: 1) All latency-critical routes (p99 target <=130ms) pinned to ORD reserved pool; 2) Embeddings + offline re-ranks allow AMS reserved + spot for burst; 3) Auto-fallback: if AMS spot preemptions > threshold -> shift burst to ORD overflow (if capacity exists).
Sahil (infra): addition — we should enable cross-region prefix cache for prompt KV to reduce repeated token compute when routing to AMS. saves ~6-8% token cost.
Jim K: ops note: config changes needed in router policy: add priority weights, fallback TTL, and capacity guardrails. I can draft PR.
Alex W: sample router snippet I tested: 
```yaml
routes:
  - name: live-inference
    regions: [ord]
    priority: 10
    fallback: [ams]
  - name: batch-embeddings
    regions: [ams, ord]
    priority: 5
    spot_allowed: true
```
Maria T: what's the recommended commit size for AMS to make it worthwhile?
Ravi S: based on current utilization profile, committing ~200 A6000-equivalent hours/mo in AMS reduces blended per-token cost by ~11% vs on-demand; 500 hours/mo is needed for the 16% tier.
Nina F: ok please create a short finance request with expected savings and risk bullets. I need the expected delta in monthly burn and the rollback plan.
Alex W: will do. action items: 1) Jim to open router policy PR (ETA EOD) 2) Ravi to model commit sizes and invoice impact (ETA Tue) 3) Maria + Nina to approve finance request (sync Wed) 4) Sahil to prototype KV prefix caching in AMS route (ETA next week)
Sahil (infra): quick perf note — if we move >30% of batch to AMS, orchestration spike may require burst capacity in ORD for fallback. budget that in.
Alex W: noted. final thought: this isn't a one-off — we should run the same runbook for APAC zones next and include GCP vs AWS differences. happier to pair on that after this round. :thumbsup:
Maria T: thanks Alex, good coverage.
Jim K: PR opened: https://repo/infra/routers/pull/412 (link placeholder) — reviews welcome
Alex W: closing for now, will follow up with the finance doc and the commit model.
